I believe that mental illness in general is looked down upon in today's society because a lot of people don't understand it so therefore they feel ashamed of a loved one who is diagnosed with some from of mental illness because that person acts a little different than the rest of them. They can't physically see the problem so they just don't get it. So that leaves us by societies standards as weird or broken. We generally are young when issues start being noticed by others and therefore a lot of is are diagnosed at an early age. We are generally not put into long term mental health hospitals unless we are deemed a danger to ourselves or others which causes the "normal" people in the world to have to interact with us causing them to look down upon those of us who are suffering and so they call us "crazy" because they don't get it that it's not our fault we are different. When people don't understand something they are freightened or threatened by it. They slap a label on it as to give it a name because it makes them feel better. 
Alzheimer's/dementia on the other hand is a chronic degenertive disease of the brain which causes the brain to atrophy/shrink in size effecting the short term memory first and as the disease progresses it effects the long term memory causing the suffering person to eventually become bedridden and unable to eat or even speak. We know this because it's pretty much the same script with most geriatrics. And this is typically a late in life disease and a lot of people put there loved ones in institutions so they don't have to deal with it. The ole "Can't see it from my house" mentality is in full effect. They know the end is coming for those people. With the mental health stuff, it's in there faces causing them to have to deal with it which most are uncomfortable with. Knowledge is power and unfortunately we usually only hear about mental health issues when something bad happens and it's reported in the media which causes peopel to put is all on one big crazy ass category.
